CORAM: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE GAUTAM KUMAR CHOUDHARY -----
For the Appellant : Mrs. J.K. Mazumdar, Advocate For the State : Mr. Jitendra Pandey, APP  -----
Oral Order 05 / Dated : 15.02.2024  Heard the parties.
1. The judgment of conviction and order of sentence under Section 376 of Indian Penal Code is under challenge in the instant criminal appeal.
2. The informant of the case is the father of the victim girl aged about 5 years.

As per the FIR, on 12.01.2009, in the evening at 8:30 pm when minor victim girl was sitting outside her house, she was enticed away and was taken behind block office where she was undressed and rape was committed with her as a result, there was bleeding injury on her private part.
When the father of the victim went to the house of the accused, he was assaulted.
Barkatha P.S. case No. 12 of 2009 was registered under Section 376 of Indian Penal Code against the appellant.
3. The police after investigation submitted charge-sheet and after cognizance the accused was put on trial under Section 376 of Indian Penal Code.
4. Altogether seven witnesses were examined and the medico legally examination report and other documents were marked as exhibits.

5. The trial Court returning the judgment of conviction by recording a finding that although hymen Suraj Vishwakarma vs The State Of Jharkhand on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192758782/
1 was found intact but it is not necessary to complete penetration and rupture of hymen to make out the offence of rape.
6. The judgment of conviction and order of sentence has been assailed on the ground that the victim was examined as PW3 and she has not stated that the rape was committed with her.

sentences.text: In para 15 she has deposed to the Court's question of putting cross-examination that what had been done by the accused about her she said that nothing was done to her.

It is further argued that the medical legally examination was adduced into evidence and marked as Ext.2 in which the allegation of rape is not supported as the hymen was not torn and no spermatozoa was found to be smeared.
7. Learned counsel for the State has defended the impugned judgment of conviction and order of sentence.
8. This is yet another case where a minor girl aged five years has become a victim of sexual assault.
FIR has been lodged without any delay.
The victim was 4 to 5 years of age at the time of her evidence and deposed that in no uncertain term she was taken by the appellant to the Block where she was undressed and rape was committed.
She has reiterated in para 6 of her deposition that some wrong was committed with her after removing her cloths.
9. In para 8 of her cross-examination, she has stated that when she was being taken, no one had seen her.
Her testimony is corroborated by her mother PW2 who deposed that her daughter was enticed away on a promise to give some snacks.
She was taken near Barkatha Block and rape was committed.
She returned from there weeping and said that something wrong had been done and when her mother inspected her private part, she found the blood oozing out from there.
She was cross-examined at length but there is no material to suggest that there was any motive to falsely implicate the appellant in the case.
There was no past enmity.
The testimonies of minor girl and her mother were duly corroborated by the consistent account of other witnesses namely Geeta Devi PW1 and father PW4 and PW7.
PWs. 5 and 6, who are co-villagers, have been declared hostile but it will not have any bearing on the testimony of the victim girl and other witnesses who have supported the case.
The medico legally examination report although noticed that hymen was found intact because introitus was very small.
Doctor opined that this to be a case of rape.
It has been held in Wahid Khan v. State of M.P., (2010) 2 SCC 9 that even slightest penetration was sufficient to constitute rape.

sentences.text: The Court observed 20.

It is appropriate in this context to reproduce the opinion expressed by Modi in Medical Jurisprudence and Toxicology (22nd Edn.) at p. 495 which reads thus:
"Thus, to constitute the offence of rape, it is not necessary that there should be complete penetration of penis with emission of semen and rupture of hymen.
Partial penetration of the penis within the labia majora or the vulva or pudenda with or without emission of semen or even an attempt at penetration is quite sufficient for the purpose of the law.
It is therefore quite possible to commit legally, the offence of rape without producing any injury to the genitals or leaving any seminal stains.

In such a case, the medical officer should mention the negative facts in his report, but Suraj Vishwakarma vs The State Of Jharkhand on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192758782/
2 should not give his opinion that no rape had been committed.

sentences.text: Rape is a crime and not a medical condition.
Rape is a legal term and not a diagnosis to be made by the medical officer treating the victim.
The only statement that can be made by the medical officer is to the effect whether there is evidence of recent sexual activity.
Whether the rape has occurred or not is a legal conclusion, not a medical one."
(emphasis supplied)
I do not find any infirmity in the finding recorded by the trial court and the reasoning given that rupture of hymen is not an essential requirement to constitute rape.
The judgment of conviction passed by the trial court is affirmed considering the nature of offence.
The sentence does not need any interference.
The appeal is dismissed and the appellant's bail is cancelled.
He is directed to surrender before the court below within two weeks to serve the remaining part of sentence.
